product.name: Symphony
notFor: not a multi-tenant control plane, workflow engine, or mandated sandbox product
not for ambiguous high-judgment interactive Codex work

sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `symphony`
- Canonical name: Symphony (`claim-symphony-sf-identity`)
- Vendor: OpenAI (`claim-symphony-sf-vendor`)
- Canonical URL: https://openai.com/index/open-source-codex-orchestration-symphony/ (`claim-symphony-sf-canonical-url`)
- Public repository: https://github.com/openai/symphony (`claim-symphony-sf-repository-url`)
- Current status: engineering preview for trusted environments (`claim-symphony-sf-status-preview`); announcement says it is a reference implementation not planned as a standalone product (`claim-symphony-sf-status-reference`); GitHub repo is public and unarchived (`claim-symphony-sf-status-public`); SPEC.md is Draft v1 (`claim-symphony-sf-spec-status`)
- Checked version: GitHub Release v0.0.2 dated 2026-07-24 (`claim-symphony-sf-version`)
- Availability: Burrito targets macos_arm64, macos_x86_64, linux_arm64, linux_x86_64 (`claim-symphony-sf-availability`)
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-15

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: an agent orchestrator that turns an issue tracker into a control plane for coding agents (`claim-symphony-sf-what-it-is`); SPEC.md calls it a scheduler/runner and tracker reader that creates a per-issue workspace and runs a coding agent there (`claim-symphony-sf-what-it-is-spec`)
- What it is not: a rich multi-tenant control plane, a general-purpose workflow engine, or a product with a mandated sandbox/approval posture (`claim-symphony-sf-what-it-is-not`); not a first-party Symphony mobile client (`claim-symphony-sf-mobile-access`); not a maintained standalone product per the announcement (`claim-symphony-sf-status-reference`)

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `orchestrator` (`claim-symphony-sf-primary-type`)
- Agent-loop owner: Codex app-server owns the model-tool loop; Symphony owns poll/claim/dispatch and workspaces (`claim-symphony-sf-agent-loop-owner`)
- Architecture: workflow loader, config, tracker adapter, orchestrator, workspace manager, agent runner, optional status surface, logging (`claim-symphony-sf-architecture`)
- Lineage: language-agnostic `SPEC.md` plus an experimental Elixir reference implementation (`claim-symphony-sf-lineage`)

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-symphony-cli`, `surface-symphony-dashboard`, `surface-symphony-api`
- Execution location: default same-device per-issue workspace (`claim-symphony-sf-execution-local`); optional SSH remote worker hosts (`claim-symphony-sf-execution-ssh`); announcement describes an always-on host/devbox daemon (`claim-symphony-sf-execution-devboxes`)

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: model selection is a Codex command/config concern (`claim-symphony-sf-model-strategy`)
- Auth strategy: host-side tracker secrets and host Codex auth; tracker tokens are stripped from the Codex child (`claim-symphony-sf-auth-strategy`, `claim-symphony-sf-reuses-auth-codex`)
- Provider support: Codex family via app-server (`claim-symphony-sf-provider-support`); Elixir adapters for Linear, GitHub Issues, Jira Cloud, Asana, and GitLab (`claim-symphony-sf-tracker-adapters`)

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: repo-owned `WORKFLOW.md` prompt template rendered with issue fields (`claim-symphony-sf-context-behavior`)
- Memory: per-issue workspace reuse; no separate memory product established (`claim-symphony-sf-memory`)
- Compaction: unknown (`claim-symphony-sf-compaction`)
- Session behavior: in-worker continuation turns plus a short continuation retry (`claim-symphony-sf-session-behavior`); in-memory scheduler state is not restored on restart (`claim-symphony-sf-session-restart`)

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: host-executed tracker tools `linear_graphql`, `github_api`, `jira_rest`, `asana_api`, `gitlab_api` (`claim-symphony-sf-tools`)
- Extensions: optional HTTP server and SSH worker extensions (`claim-symphony-sf-extensions`)
- MCP: announcement uses Codex dynamic tool calls for Linear, not MCP (`claim-symphony-sf-mcp`)
- Skills: optional `commit`, `push`, `pull`, `land`, and `linear` skills (`claim-symphony-sf-skills`)
- Hooks: `after_create`, `before_run`, `after_run`, `before_remove` (`claim-symphony-sf-hooks`)
- APIs: optional `/api/v1/state`, `/api/v1/<issue_identifier>`, `/api/v1/refresh` (`claim-symphony-sf-api`)

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: single-authority poll/claim/dispatch/retry/reconcile loop (`claim-symphony-sf-orchestration`)
- Parallelism: bounded concurrent per-issue agents (`claim-symphony-sf-parallelism`)
- Capability tags written: `wraps-cli`, `parallel-agents`, `hooks`, `background` (`claim-symphony-sf-tag-wraps-cli`, `claim-symphony-sf-tag-parallel-agents`, `claim-symphony-sf-tag-hooks`, `claim-symphony-sf-tag-background`)

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: sanitized per-issue workspace path inside `workspace.root` (`claim-symphony-sf-isolation`)
- Permissions: SPEC.md leaves approval/sandbox implementation-defined (`claim-symphony-sf-permissions-spec`); Elixir omitted defaults reject approvals and use workspace-write (`claim-symphony-sf-permissions`)
- Security: trusted-environment preview (`claim-symphony-sf-security`)
- Data path: host-side tracker secrets; child workspace plus Codex session (`claim-symphony-sf-data-path`)

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
List each surface from `surfaces.jsonl` separately. Native mobile, first-party mobile web, first-party messaging, vendor relay, remote client, private-network, Termux/mobile terminal, and generic remote shell stay distinct.

- Interface and surface IDs:
  - Local CLI / Burrito executable: `surface-symphony-cli` (`claim-symphony-sf-surface-cli`)
  - Optional same-host Phoenix dashboard: `surface-symphony-dashboard` (`claim-symphony-sf-surface-dashboard`)
  - Optional same-host JSON API: `surface-symphony-api` (`claim-symphony-sf-surface-api`)
- Remote behavior: optional SSH workers for remote Codex execution; no first-party remoting client (`claim-symphony-sf-remote-access`, `claim-symphony-sf-execution-ssh`)
- Mobile behavior: Linear-app task intake in the announcement; no first-party Symphony mobile client established (`claim-symphony-sf-mobile-access`)
- Background behavior: long-running poll-loop daemon (`claim-symphony-sf-background`)

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: unknown; no Symphony SKU on the announcement (`claim-symphony-sf-pricing`)
- License: Apache-2.0 (`claim-symphony-sf-license`)
- Maintenance: announcement says not planned as a maintained standalone product (`claim-symphony-sf-maintenance-blog`); public repo last pushed 2026-08-12 (`claim-symphony-sf-maintenance-repo`); latest release v0.0.2 (`claim-symphony-sf-version`)
- Lock-in: Apache-2.0 spec intended to be reimplemented (`claim-symphony-sf-lock-in`, `claim-symphony-sf-license`); runtime still launches Codex app-server (`claim-symphony-sf-wraps-cli-codex`)

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: spec plus experimental Elixir reference implementation (`claim-symphony-sf-lineage`)
- Relationship edges:
  - `symphony --orchestrates--> codex-family` (`claim-symphony-sf-orchestrates-codex`)
  - `symphony --wraps_cli--> codex-family` (`claim-symphony-sf-wraps-cli-codex`)
  - `symphony --reuses_auth_from--> codex-family` (`claim-symphony-sf-reuses-auth-codex`)

sections.heading: Closest substitutes, partial substitutes, same-lineage relatives, often-confused products, and complements
sections.body:
Use `comparison-neighborhoods.jsonl` memberships. None were written.

- Comparison neighborhood IDs: unknown
- Substitutes: unknown
- Partial substitutes: unknown
- Same-lineage relatives: unknown
- Often-confused products: unknown
- Complements: Codex family is the orchestrated runtime, not a neighborhood membership (`claim-symphony-sf-provider-support`)

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: issue-tracker control plane plus an open orchestration spec (`claim-symphony-sf-unique`)
- Meaningful drawbacks: prototype/evaluation-only Elixir implementation (`claim-symphony-sf-drawback-preview`); no mid-flight steering (`claim-symphony-sf-drawback-no-midflight`); trusted-environment preview (`claim-symphony-sf-status-preview`)
- Best fit: teams with harness-engineered repos who want to manage work rather than supervise agents (`claim-symphony-sf-intended-user`)
- Not-for: ambiguous high-judgment interactive Codex work (`claim-symphony-sf-not-for`); not a multi-tenant control plane or mandated-sandbox product (`claim-symphony-sf-what-it-is-not`)

sections.body:

### Unresolved contradictions

- Announcement says Symphony will not be maintained as a standalone product (`claim-symphony-sf-status-reference`, `claim-symphony-sf-maintenance-blog`) versus a public unarchived repo with v0.0.2 and a 2026-08-12 push (`claim-symphony-sf-status-public`, `claim-symphony-sf-version`, `claim-symphony-sf-maintenance-repo`).
- Announcement is Linear-centric (`claim-symphony-sf-identity`) versus Elixir README multi-tracker adapters (`claim-symphony-sf-tracker-adapters`).
- SPEC.md is Draft v1 (`claim-symphony-sf-spec-status`) versus Elixir/GitHub Release v0.0.2 (`claim-symphony-sf-version`).
- SPEC.md leaves approval/sandbox implementation-defined (`claim-symphony-sf-permissions-spec`) versus Elixir safer omitted defaults (`claim-symphony-sf-permissions`).
- SPEC.md non-goals include a rich web UI (`claim-symphony-sf-what-it-is-not`) versus the optional Phoenix dashboard (`claim-symphony-sf-surface-dashboard`).
